label: Technology Index (equal-weight composite of XLK, VGT, FTEC)
appendOnly: Points are only ever added, never edited. Once a point is more than one year older than the latest collection, only the last point of its Monday–Sunday week is kept (unchanged) and the week's other points are dropped. Later source differences for a kept point are listed under revisions.
basis: Index level (base 100) recomputed from each constituent's Cboe daily close on the point's date.

granularity.rule: Points dated more than one year before the latest collection are weekly: the last point of each Monday–Sunday week (for markets, the week's last trading-day close), labelled with its own date. Points within the last year are as published (daily) or as collected. A week with no point is a gap — nothing is interpolated or filled.

backfill.note: Computed from Cboe's published daily closes of each constituent, back to 2013-10-24, the first date all of XLK, VGT, FTEC have a Cboe close (set by FTEC); base 100 = close of 2025-10-06.

source.name: Cboe delayed quotes (daily closes), computed by this collector

methodology.construction: Bower Digital composite — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or tracking any provider's index.
methodology.value: 100 × mean over constituents of (close on t ÷ close on base date): an equal-weight basket bought at the base close and held, no rebalancing.
methodology.d1: Mean of the constituents' 1-day price returns from the previous common close, in %. On weekly points the previous close is not stored in this file; it is the prior common Cboe close.
methodology.returnBasis: Price return from split-adjusted daily closes; distributions not included.
methodology.backHistory: Same three funds, same weights, same base, back to the first common close. Each fund held what its sector meant at the time: before the 2016 split of Real Estate out of Financials, the 2018 creation of Communication Services (Alphabet and Meta moved out of Information Technology; telecom funds became communication-services funds) and the 2023 move of payment companies such as Visa and Mastercard from Information Technology to Financials.
